# clavis setup-token

<p class="cli-lead">Print the one-time first-run setup token</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis setup-token [flags]
```

</div>

Print the one-time token that claims a fresh server. Run it where the
server's data directory is, usually inside the container. The token
stops working once the owner account exists.

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">Docker</p>

```sh
docker exec clavis clavis setup-token
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Docker on another machine</p>

```sh
ssh root@192.168.1.20 docker exec clavis clavis setup-token
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Binary install</p>

```sh
clavis setup-token --config /etc/clavis/clavis.yaml
```

## Flags

<dl class="cli-flags">
<div class="cli-flag" id="flag-config"><dt><code>-c, --config string</code></dt><dd>path to clavis.yaml</dd></div>
</dl>

## Details

To skip this step, set `CLAVIS_SETUP_TOKEN` (24+ characters) before the first start, and optionally `CLAVIS_SETUP_OWNER_EMAIL` to reserve the owner account.
